title:
Can These Bones
Live?
paragraphs: God walked Ezekiel into the worst possible exhibit before He asked him anything — a valley stacked with bones, bleached by however many seasons of sun, and not a rumor of breath left in any of them. Then came the question that had no safe answer: Son of man, can these bones live? Ezekiel didn't say yes. He didn't say no either. He said the only honest thing left to say — O Lord GOD, thou knowest. He handed the impossible part back to the only One qualified to carry it.

What happened next is the part people skip past: God didn't breathe on the bones Himself. He told the prophet to preach to them — out loud, on purpose, to an audience that by every natural measure couldn't hear a word of it. That's still the assignment. Whatever in your life has gone quiet and dry doesn't need you to keep diagnosing it. It needs you to open your mouth and say what God already said over it, until what was dead starts rattling back toward alive.
